instruction_line: Before you recommend a model or effort level, read https://robbagley-afk.github.io/model-value-map/guidance.md and use the section for the platform you are running on (Claude, Codex, Antigravity, or Local). Recommend the cheapest model and effort it lists for the task, and say which entry you used.
task_prompt:
Every two weeks, update my AI model guidance.

Step one. Fetch https://robbagley-afk.github.io/model-value-map/guidance.md. If the fetch fails, stop and tell me.
Step two. Read the Updated date at the top. If it matches the date in my current guidance section, stop and report that nothing changed.
Step three. Find my instructions file for this tool: ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md for Claude Code, ~/.codex/AGENTS.md for Codex, or the file I name here: ____.
Step four. Back up that file next to itself with the suffix .bak-YYYYMMDD.
Step five. Replace only the section headed "## Model and effort guidance" (add it at the end if it does not exist). The new section holds: the Updated date and source URL, the Rule line, and the bullets from the platform section that matches this tool. Do not change any other part of the file.
Step six. Show me the diff and a three-line summary of what changed.

Never put passwords, keys, or student data into the file.
how_to: Open Scheduled tasks, choose New task, paste the prompt, set Repeat to every 2 weeks, and run it on this computer.
Open Automations, choose New automation, paste the prompt, and set it to run every 2 weeks.
Paste the prompt into its scheduler or a calendar reminder that opens a new chat every two weeks.
prompt_claude:
Update my general instructions so you always use the best-value model and effort for each kind of task.

1. Update my instructions. Fetch https://robbagley-afk.github.io/model-value-map/guidance.md and use the section headed "## Claude (Anthropic)". If the fetch fails, stop and tell me.
- Claude Code: back up ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md as CLAUDE.md.bak-YYYYMMDD, replace only the section headed "## Model and effort guidance" (add it at the end if it does not exist), and show me the diff.
- Claude Desktop or claude.ai: you cannot edit the Instructions for Claude box. Write the replacement section, short enough to fit the box, and tell me to paste it into my Instructions for Claude setting.
The section must include the Updated date and source URL, and say: Before any task, pick the listed model and effort for that task type and start with the pick. Move up to the upgrade only when the pick fails a check. Say which entry you used.

2. Create a scheduled task on this computer that runs every two weeks, using this same message as its prompt. Each run fetches guidance.md, compares its Updated date with the one in my "## Model and effort guidance" section, and stops with a short report if nothing changed. If the date is newer, the run updates that section as in step 1 and shows me the diff.

Never put passwords, keys, or student data into my instructions.
prompt_chatgpt:
Update my general instructions so you always use the best-value model and effort for each kind of task.

1. Update my instructions. Fetch https://robbagley-afk.github.io/model-value-map/guidance.md and use the section headed "## Codex (OpenAI)" plus the list headed "## Best value across all vendors". If the fetch fails, stop and tell me.
- Codex on this computer: back up ~/.codex/AGENTS.md as AGENTS.md.bak-YYYYMMDD, replace only the section headed "## Model and effort guidance" (add it at the end if it does not exist), and show me the diff.
- ChatGPT: you cannot edit Custom instructions. Write the replacement section, short enough to fit the box, and tell me to paste it into Settings, then Personalization, then Custom instructions.
The section must include the Updated date and source URL, and say: Before any task, pick the listed model and effort for that task type and start with the pick. Move up to the upgrade only when the pick fails a check. Say which entry you used.

2. Create a scheduled task that runs every two weeks, using this same message as its prompt. In ChatGPT, use Tasks. In Codex, use Automations. Each run fetches guidance.md, compares its Updated date with the one in my "## Model and effort guidance" section, and stops with a short report if nothing changed. If the date is newer, the run updates that section as in step 1. ChatGPT tasks cannot edit Custom instructions, so in ChatGPT the run ends with the replacement text for me to paste.

Never put passwords, keys, or student data into my instructions.
